A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from LegoGPT to BrickGPT. All 16 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on 250 prompts, quantitative baseline comparisons and ablations in Table 1, novelty analysis, and demonstrations of robotic and manual assembly.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and assembly demonstrations and adds DINOv2 image-similarity results to Table 1.

M1.justification: The LLaMA backbone, fine-tuning approach, brick representation, rejection sampling, physics-aware rollback, and texturing procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A expands the existing mesh-conversion heuristics under the name delete-and-rebuild; this supplies implementation detail without establishing a replacement procedure.

E1.justification: StableText2Lego is renamed StableText2Brick, retaining the same ShapeNetCore coverage, 21 categories, grid resolution, and dataset counts. Text generation, coloring/texturing, and robotic/manual assembly remain the evaluated tasks. DINOv2 adds a metric rather than new data coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains zero-shot and five-shot LLaMA, LLaMA-Mesh, LGM, XCube, and Hunyuan3D-2. Image2Lego is not evaluated in either version; removing the explanation for its omission does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds cosine similarity between DINOv2 features of rendered generated and ground-truth structures for the same prompt, evaluated on valid structures. The existing metrics, 90/10 split, 250-prompt evaluation, model size, and stated training and inference budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing rejection-sampling and rollback ablations gain DINOv2 measurements, extending evidence about their effect on shape fidelity. No ablation factor is added; Figure 6 examples and the appendix novelty analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report one generated design per evaluation prompt and aggregate scores without repeated-run statistics, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added DINOv2 results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds DINOv2 scores, including 0.880 for the full method and 0.868 for Hunyuan3D-2. LLaMA-Mesh CLIP changes from 0.311 to 0.317 and LGM from 0.299 to 0.300, without explanation. Existing validity and stability values, including the full method's 100% validity and 98.8% stability, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, equilibrium assumptions, stability-score definition, collision constraint, and inference algorithm retain their mathematical content. Equation 3 changes delimiter sizing, not its objective. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: stable and buildable text-conditioned generation, a captioned dataset, appearance generation, and human/robot assembly. Generic interconnecting-brick terminology accompanies the rebranding without introducing a distinct scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly contrasts the method's retained 21-category coverage with the wider object variety supported by other 3D generators. v2 also removes the explanation that Image2Lego was not compared because its code was unavailable. The main mechanism explanations and remaining limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A expands mesh-conversion details with bottom-to-top construction, support/connectivity/orientation priorities, explicit weak-region deletion and rebuilding, and random region selection and tie breaking. Training hyperparameters and hardware remain unchanged. The project access pointer changes from LegoGPT to BrickGPT.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to octree-based autoregressive generation, Funes and Pollack's evolutionary physical design, DINOv2, and Wang et al.'s visual-manual planning, while removing Atlas3D. Related work gains a manual-planning sentence and drops the characterization of physics-constrained generation as largely unexplored.

P1.justification: The title, method/dataset names, and terminology change throughout, accompanied by grammatical edits and localized paragraph rewrites, particularly in Appendix A. The section order and overall narrative structure remain intact; widespread name replacement does not amount to a major reorganization.

P2.justification: Table 1 adds a DINO column and removes metric-direction arrows. Figures retain their examples while updating embedded labels and captions for the rebranding. Local spacing and text placement change, but no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 supplements CLIP with reference-image similarity evidence in Table 1 and makes Appendix A's mesh-to-brick construction more reproducible. These are limited gains around unchanged central results. Removing the explanation for omitting Image2Lego slightly reduces transparency, but the added evaluation evidence and implementation detail support a modest net improvement.
